claim: Telegraf's MQTT output plugin defaults keep_alive to 0, but mosquitto v2.0.12+ rejects zero keep-alive connections with 'identifier rejected', so a non-zero keep_alive is mandatory against modern mosquitto brokers
stance_target: ha-linux-agent must configure an explicit non-zero MQTT keep-alive (rumqttc's zero/disabled keep-alive default is unsafe)
scope_conditions: Telegraf MQTT Producer output plugin; mosquitto >= v2.0.12; MQTT 3.1.1/5
quoted_support: In v2.0.12+ of the mosquitto MQTT server, there is a bug requiring the keep_alive value to be set non-zero in Telegraf. Otherwise, the server will return with identifier rejected. As a reference eclipse/paho.golang sets the keep_alive to 30.

claim: Telegraf's MQTT output cannot set a dynamic MQTT last-will (LWT), so Homie-layout devices are only marked 'lost' on clean Telegraf exit and stay wrongly 'ready' after crashes or abnormal aborts
stance_target: ha-linux-agent's LWT-based availability design is a genuine differentiator over the incumbent Telegraf pattern; LWT must be set at CONNECT time
scope_conditions: Telegraf MQTT output homie-v4 layout; limitation attributed to the MQTT client library
quoted_support: Due to limitations in the MQTT client library, it is not possible to set a "will" dynamically. In consequence, devices are only marked lost when exiting Telegraf normally and might not change in abnormal aborts.

claim: Telegraf's Homie layout suffers device/node/property churn because Telegraf metrics are not known a priori — $nodes and $properties topic contents change as metrics appear/disappear, especially during startup
stance_target: a purpose-built agent with a fixed, declared sensor set gives stable entity identity where Telegraf's generic pipeline cannot
quoted_support: It is important to notice that the "devices" and "nodes" are dynamically changing in Telegraf as the metrics and their structure is not known a-priori. As a consequence, the content of both $nodes and $properties topics are changing as new device-ids, node-ids, and properties (tags and fields) appear.

claim: Telegraf's Homie ID conversion (lower-case, forbidden characters replaced by hyphen, leading/trailing hyphens removed) creates a risk of name collisions between fields and tags of the same node, causing property topics to be sent multiple times
stance_target: stable entity naming needs deliberate design; naive normalisation collides
scope_conditions: Telegraf MQTT output homie-v4 layout; Homie topic ID spec
quoted_support: This is important as there is a risk of name collisions between fields and tags of the same node especially after the conversion to ID. Please make sure to avoid those collisions as otherwise property topics will be sent multiple times for the colliding items.

claim: Telegraf MQTT output publishes to Go-template topics (default 'telegraf/{{ .Tag "host" }}/{{ .Name }}') with Sprig functions and env vars allowed per path segment; empty path segments and MQTT wildcard characters (+ or #) in topics cause errors
stance_target: topic-naming conventions available to an MQTT publisher; host-templated topic trees are the established pattern
quoted_support: Each path segment accepts either a template placeholder, an environment variable, or a tag key of the form `{{.Tag "tag_key_name"}}`. All the functions provided by the Sprig library are available. Empty path elements as well as special MQTT characters (such as `+` or `#`) are invalid to form the topic name and will lead to an error.

claim: Telegraf MQTT output defaults to QoS 2 (exactly once), supports protocols 3.1.1 (default) and 5, generates a random client_id when unset, and has a 5s default write timeout
stance_target: operational defaults of the incumbent MQTT publisher to compare agent defaults against
quoted_support: ## Protocol can be `3.1.1` or `5`. Default is `3.1.1` ... ## QoS policy for messages ... # qos = 2 ... ## The unique client id to connect MQTT server. If this parameter is not set then a random ID is generated. ... ## Timeout for write operations. default: 5s

claim: Telegraf's 'field' MQTT layout publishes one topic per metric field containing only the value as a string, ignoring data_format and omitting tags and timestamps entirely
stance_target: per-field topic layout is a viable MQTT sensor pattern (value-as-string on leaf topics), but loses metadata
scope_conditions: Telegraf MQTT Producer output, field layout
quoted_support: This layout will publish one topic per metric field, only containing the value as string. This means that the data_format option will be ignored. ... NOTE: Only fields will be output, tags and the timestamp are omitted.

claim: Telegraf MQTT output requires TLS and non-TLS brokers to not be mixed in the servers list, and mandatory homie_device_name / homie_node_id templates must not contain slashes in the homie-v4 layout
stance_target: configuration constraints of the incumbent pattern
quoted_support: Scheme can be any of the following: tcp://, mqtt://, tls://, mqtts:// non-TLS and TLS servers can not be mix-and-matched. ... The following options provide templates for setting the device name and the node-ID for the topics. Both options are MANDATORY ... Templates MAY NOT contain slashes!
